title: Kangaroo Tail candlestick pattern detector
description: A 3-bar reversal pattern from Elder ch. 20 ('fingers'), completely separate from anything in this codebase (no candlestick-pattern detection exists at all). Definition, purely from OHLC: a single bar whose range is roughly 2-3x the recent average bar range, protruding from a tight recent range, where the close ends up back near the open (not at the extreme) -- flanked by two bars of normal height. An upward-pointing tail (new high, closes back down) = bearish reversal; a downward-pointing tail (new low, closes back up) = bullish reversal. Stop placement is explicit in the source: halfway through the tail, not at its tip (too wide) or base (too tight) -- expose this as a suggested reference level alongside the flag, not just a boolean.

checklist.step: Decide and record the exact 'average bar range' baseline (lookback window, and the multiplier threshold for what counts as a tail -- book says roughly 2-3x, pick and justify a specific number).
Implement detection for both directions (upward/downward tail) plus the confirming-next-bar check.
Implement the halfway-through-the-tail suggested stop reference.
Tests reproducing the book's own worked examples (BIIB upward tail, FDO downward tail) as closely as fixture data allows.
Expose as a flag (+ direction + suggested stop reference) on the analysis/indicator-history responses; regenerate openapi.json/frontend types; document in docs/Analyse.md.
